ruling.recommended_action: Refund $2.56 to the rider's original payment method for the unnotified surge increase; no driver violation recorded (no route deviation, RD-4 screen: none).
ruling.reasoning:
This is a fare dispute about the surge multiplier, not a route dispute. The GPS and fare records show actual distance 4.0 km against an optimal route of 4.0 km, +0.0 km, so billed distance does not exceed the optimal route [F1][F3] and no excess-distance component arises under RD-2's distance matrix. The money therefore turns solely on the surge change: quote $15.63 at 1.2× [F6], trip metered at 1.5× for $18.19 [F7], i.e. $2.56 above the quote [F8].

Under SURGE-2 the trigger is whether the rider was notified of the rise. The only notice on the record is the in-app message logged at 18:29:30 [F9], while the trip started at 18:27:00 and lasted 6.8 min [F2][F5]; the code's trace marks the "notified in-app at or before pickup" element as failed on that record [F9]. The chat record contains only pickup logistics at 18:23 and 18:24 [F10][F11], every message timestamped [F12], and nothing about the price change; the driver's post-trip statement that he does not set the price [F13] cannot supply notice. Notice given after the trip has begun is not notice "before or at pickup" under SURGE-1, so the rider was not notified and SURGE-2 gives the surge differential back.

Amount: the differential computation is (1.5 − 1.2) × $11.29 = $3.39 [F8], capped at the $2.56 by which the actual fare exceeds the quote [F8], and the trace fixes the amount as (1.5 − 0.2 difference) × surgeable subtotal = $2.56. Booking fee $1.25 is not surged [F7], so nothing outside the surge is refundable. Refund: $2.56, `refund_partial`.

The rider's fraud flag (flagged_for_repeated_fare_disputes) [F14] is expressly excluded from deciding the case; no account action against either party is called for. The driver has one upheld dispute in 90 days and no route or no-show violations [F15], and no deviation violation can be recorded here since the route matched the optimal one [F1][F3].

element_findings.reason: The only notice in the record is the in-app message at 18:29:30 [F9], sent after the 18:27:00 trip start (trip 6.8 min [F2]); SURGE-1 requires notice before or at pickup, so on timing alone the notice is not met even though the wording states the 1.5× multiplier, the revised fare and free cancellation [F9].
Surge rose from 1.2× [F6] to 1.5× [F7] and the rider was not notified before or at pickup [F9]; SURGE-2 directs full refund of the surge differential.
(1.5 − 1.2) × $11.29 = $3.39 capped at the $2.56 by which the $18.19 fare exceeds the $15.63 quote [F8]; booking fee $1.25 not surged [F7].

rejected_claims.reason: The three SURGE-1 items may be quoted from F9, but SURGE-1 requires the notice before or at pickup; the notice is time-stamped 18:29:30 against an 18:27:00 start [F9][F2], so correct wording cannot cure the timing defect under SURGE-1.

The chat contains only pickup logistics at 18:23 and 18:24 [F10][F11][F12]; rider silence is not acceptance of the higher multiplier, and the only price message on the record is the late system notice [F9] (SURGE-1).
The rider's fraud flag [F14] affects only the TH-3 threshold; it cannot decide the case, and the driver's own record [F15] is not a defence to the SURGE-1 notice failure.
Conceded by the driver and confirmed: nothing in the complaint, chat or statement [F10][F11][F12][F13] raises any SAFE-1 indicator, so no escalation arises under SAFE-1.
